title: The teaching of the Buddhas
hook: a kid in the back seat wants the whole path in one sentence; one verse has it
tomorrow: a chant of praise that says don't take its word. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, na hi verena verani: hatred never ends by hatred. Same book today, the Dhammapada, and a verse that tries to hold the whole path.
screen: `NA HI VERENA VERANI.` → `SAME BOOK, A BIGGER VERSE.`

segments.voice: School pickup. The line of cars hasn't moved in five minutes, and the eight-year-old in the back seat is out of snacks and full of questions. So what is Buddhism? In one sentence. Go. The parent at the wheel opens their mouth, and nothing short comes out. Meditation, kind of. Karma, sort of. Not exactly a god. The car ahead finally rolls forward. Here's the thing: the tradition has a verse built for exactly that moment, four short lines in Pali that monks and grandparents can say from memory. You walked around a temple with it last year at Magha Puja. Today it gets taken apart, word by word.
screen: `STUCK IN PICKUP.` → `BUDDHISM, IN ONE SENTENCE?` → `FOUR SHORT LINES IN PALI.`

segments.voice: Line one: sabbapapassa akaranam. Sabba, all. Papa, evil, the harmful thing done. Akaranam, not-doing. Not doing any evil. Notice it starts with a not: before anything grand, stop adding harm. Line two: kusalassa upasampada. Kusala is the skillful, the wholesome; upasampada is taking it up, arriving at it. Taking up the good. Now there's something to do, not only something to skip. Line three: sacittapariyodapanam. Sa-citta, your own mind; pariyodapanam, making it clear, washing it clean. Clearing your own mind. Your own, not your neighbor's. Line four: etam buddhana sasanam. Etam, this. Buddhana, of the Buddhas, plural. Sasanam, the teaching. Max Müller's old translation runs: "Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened." He chose sin for papa, an English word with a long history of its own; the Pali sits closer to harm, the bad thing done. And keep an eye on that plural. In the verse, this isn't one teacher's private rule; it's what awakened ones teach. So, back to the car. Stop the harm. Take up the good. Clear your own mind. It fits between two traffic lights, and it holds a whole life.
screen: `SABBAPAPASSA AKARANAM: NOT DOING ANY EVIL.` · `KUSALASSA UPASAMPADA: TAKING UP THE GOOD.` · `SACITTAPARIYODAPANAM: CLEARING YOUR MIND.` · `ETAM BUDDHANA SASANAM: THE BUDDHAS' TEACHING.` · then, large: `THE HEART IN PALI.`

segments.voice: Chant the whole verse slowly, one line to a breath: sabbapapassa akaranam; kusalassa upasampada; sacittapariyodapanam; etam buddhana sasanam. Rest in the quiet after the last word. Then chant it once more, a little softer, and let the sit carry the rest.
The teaching of the Buddhas: etam buddhana sasanam. Not doing evil, taking up the good, clearing your own mind, in four short lines.
screen: `THE TEACHING OF THE BUDDHAS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the heart in Pali. Short enough for a car ride, deep enough for a lifetime. Seventeen days of Pali, and counting.

screen: `DAY 1443 COUNTS.` → `A LITTLE PALI · 17 OF 29.` → `TOMORROW: A CHANT OF PRAISE THAT SAYS DON'T TAKE ITS WORD. WHY?`

howItsDone: Theravada Buddhists chant this Dhammapada verse in Pali at temples and at home, and it is recited at Magha Puja, the full-moon day that remembers the gathering where tradition says the Buddha first taught it.

fork.setup: your little cousin needs 'what Buddhists believe, in one sentence' for a school worksheet, due tomorrow. which line fits the verse?
options: don't add harm, take up the good, and clear your own mind.
sit still and empty your mind until nothing can bother you.

fork.reveal: the verse gives three moves, in order: stop the harm, take up the good, clear your own mind. it calls that the teaching of the Buddhas.

original.note: Pali, the verse's first line in Devanagari letters: sabba, all; papa, evil; akaranam, not-doing.

trapdoor: what you thought: a short Buddhist rule about not sinning.
what it means: three moves, in order: not doing any evil, taking up the good, clearing your own mind; this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
what a scholar hears: Müller chose 'sin' for papa, a word loaded in English; and buddhana is plural, so the verse speaks for awakened ones, not one teacher.

chat.meaning: The verse has three moves: stop the harm, take up the good, clear your own mind. Only the first one is a not.

notes: Müller quotation (Dhammapada 183, SBE X, 1881) copied with his parenthesis '(all)'; confirm exact wording and punctuation against the 1881 text.

Word glosses (sabba, papa, akarana, kusala, upasampada, sa-citta, pariyodapana, buddhanam, sasana) follow the PTS dictionary; upasampada here means 'taking up, attaining', not its other sense of full ordination. Confirm.
